carousels.caption: Gmail’s spam filter ignores ‘free’ if your sender score is high. Replies matter more than opens—here’s how to check your score and keep your emails in the inbox. #emailmarketingtips #emaildeliverability #leadgeneration #irishsmallbusiness
carousels.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your list replies
carousels.throughline: Gmail’s spam filter prioritizes sender reputation over trigger words like ‘free’—so you can use them without fear if your list is healthy.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your list replies

body.text: Gmail’s spam filter doesn’t care about trigger words like ‘free’ if your sender score is high.
It looks at how many people reply to your emails, not just open them, to decide where they go.
A sender score above 90 means Gmail skips the spam folder, even if your subject line has ‘free’ in it.
Check your sender score in Google Postmaster Tools—it’s free and takes two minutes to set up.

chart.label: inbox placement
chart.caption: Lists with high sender scores see 30% more emails land in the inbox, not spam.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your email team

body_slides.text: Gmail’s filter looks at replies, not just opens, to decide where your email lands.
A sender score above 90 means Gmail skips spam checks for words like ‘free’ or ‘discount.’
Lists with healthy sender scores see 30% more emails land in the inbox, not spam.
Check your sender score in Google Postmaster Tools—it’s free and takes two minutes.
Emails with replies move to Primary, even if the subject line says ‘free.’
The fix isn’t removing words—it’s making sure your list actually wants what you send.

carousels.caption: Google Ads wastes €0.50 on every bounce—here’s how to find and block the wasted clicks. #googleadstips #ppcmanagement #searchads #galwaybusiness
carousels.hook: Google Ads wastes €0.50 on every bounce
carousels.throughline: Google Ads charges the same for clicks that bounce as for those that convert—so you need to filter out the bounces to save money.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads bills you €0.50 for a bounce and €0.50 for a sale

body.text: Google Ads charges you the same for a click that bounces as for one that buys—no discount for bounces.
The Search Terms report shows which searches led to clicks but never converted—those are your bounces.
Most accounts waste 25% of their budget on searches that were never going to buy—block them with negatives.
Add negative keywords to stop paying for bounces—this cuts wasted spend by 30% without losing sales.

chart.label: cost per click
chart.caption: Blocking wasted clicks can cut cost per click by 30% while keeping the same conversions.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your ads manager

body_slides.text: Google Ads charges you the same for a click that bounces as for one that buys.
The Search Terms report shows which searches led to clicks but never converted.
Most accounts waste 25% of their budget on searches that were never going to buy.
Before: €0.50 per click, 10% conversion rate. After: €0.35 per click, same conversions.
Add negative keywords to block searches that bounce—this cuts wasted spend by 30%.
The fix isn’t more budget—it’s making sure every click has a chance to convert.

carousels.caption: Claude trains on everything you paste by default—unless you flip this switch. Here’s how to opt out and keep your data private. #aiforbusiness #aitoolsforbusiness #marketingaudit #corkbusiness
carousels.hook: Claude trains on everything you paste by default
carousels.throughline: Claude’s free plan keeps your pasted data forever by default—so you need to opt out to protect sensitive information.

reel_beats.hook: Claude trains on everything you paste—unless you flip this switch

body.text: Claude’s free plan trains on everything you paste—customer emails, ad copy, even passwords by default.
The default setting keeps your data forever, even after you delete your account—no opt-out by default.
Flip the ‘Data Sharing’ switch to ‘Off’ in settings—it takes 10 seconds and stops Claude from using your inputs.
Most businesses don’t know this switch exists—check yours now to keep your data private, not public.

screen.title: Turn off data sharing in Claude
screen.mechanism: Turning off data sharing stops Claude from training on your pasted data—keeps it private.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your tech team

body_slides.text: Claude’s free plan uses your pasted data—emails, ad copy, even passwords—to train its models.
The default setting keeps your data forever, even after you delete your account.
Flip ‘Data Sharing’ to ‘Off’ in settings—it takes 10 seconds and stops Claude from using your inputs.
Most businesses don’t know this switch exists—check yours now to keep data private.
Before: Data stored forever. After: Data deleted when you close the chat—no training.
The fix isn’t avoiding Claude—it’s making sure your data stays yours.

carousels.hook: Google Ads buries 17% of your buyers in one report
carousels.throughline: Google Ads hides 17% of your buyers in the ‘Other searches’ report—so you need to check it to find and target them.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads buries 17% of your buyers in one report

body.text: Google Ads groups some searches into ‘Other searches’—these are real buyers you’re missing out on.
The Search Terms report shows ‘Other searches’—click it to see the hidden buyers Google buried.
Most accounts find 17% of their best buyers hidden in this report—check yours to find them.
Add the hidden searches as keywords—this brings back the buyers Google hid and boosts your reach.

chart.caption: Checking ‘Other searches’ can bring back 17% of your hidden buyers—no extra spend needed.
